facts.text: 11 OCT 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi Six-year plan to make India self-reliant in pulses by 2030-31 India is the world's largest producer of pulses, a globally important, protein-rich food crop.
Recognising this importance, the government launched the 'Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses' on October 11, 2025.

bullets: Acidification = falling ocean pH (seawater is alkaline, pH ~8.1) from CO2 uptake; called the "evil twin of global warming" / "the other CO2 problem".
CO2 + water forms carbonic acid, which yields bicarbonate and hydronium ions; carbonate ions fall, so corals, plankton and shellfish struggle to build calcium carbonate shells (calcifying organisms).

Oceans absorb about 30-40% of anthropogenic CO2 (APP; CDI gives >25%); acidity is up 30% since the Industrial Revolution and may rise 150% by 2100. Worse in cold temperate seas (higher CO2 solubility) and the melting Arctic.

Harmful algal blooms: excess nitrogen and phosphorus (farm runoff, sewage) - eutrophication - bloom dies and decomposes - oxygen stripped - dead zones (e.g. Gulf of Mexico, Mississippi runoff; Chesapeake Bay). Blooms block sunlight for corals and seagrass.
Red tide: a toxic bloom (mostly dinoflagellates) that discolours water, kills fish and contaminates shellfish . INCOIS issues algal bloom and coral bleaching alerts.
